# GENERAL

Scope of this procedure is to define requirements, workflow and operating procedures for the management of VENDOR documentation for ABS / Rubber Plant at Assaluyeh, Iran. The procedure is issued with purpose to provide in one document the information needed by VENDORS to manage their documents in compliance with Project requirement.

# DEFINITIONS AND ACRONYMS

## ACRONYMS 

> OWNER : JAM Petrochemical Co. Iran (JPC)
>
> CONTRACTOR : JONDISHAPOUR CO. Iran (JSC)
>
> SUBCONTRACTOR :Tecnimont SpA, Milan/ Tecnimont ICB, Pvt, India (TCM/TICB)
>
> LICENSOR : Versalis SpA, Italy
>
> PM : Project Manager
>
> PCL : Project Control Lead
>
> PEM : Project Engineering Manager
>
> PE : Project Engineer
>
> DL : Discipline Leader
>
> EDMS : Electronic Document Management System
>
> DCC : Document Control Coordinator
>
> MOM : Minutes of Meeting
>

>
> IOM : Installation, Operation and Maintenance Manual
>
> CED : Equipment Certification Dossier
>

## DEFINITIONS

> **PROJECT -** means ABS & Rubber Plant
>
> **VENDOR -** means a firm awarded with a Purchase Order by CONTRACTOR to supply Equipment or Material for the PROJECT
>
> **FTP server --** means a repository, accessible through the net, to/from which it is possible to upload and download files through the FTP (File Transfer Protocol).
>
> **Document (or Documentation) -** means design documents developed by VENDORS aimed at manufacturing the equipments / materials, and may include procedure, schedule, plans, specifications, drawings, etc.
>
> **Final Documentation -** means the Manufacturers Data Book or Mechanical Catalogue to be provided by the VENDOR.

# VENDOR'S DOCUMENTATION

## Vendor's PRINT INDEX AND SCHEDULE (VPIS) 

> As per MR requirements, the VENDOR, after PO award, shall transmit for review not later than the time specified in MRQ / SRQ doocument or before the KOM, a detailed Document List, as per **Attachment 2**.
>
> Scheduled transmission date is an important part of this list, so vendor shall fulfil them without fail.
>
> Vendor to submit VPIS to the CONTRACTOR / SUB-CONTRACTOR during each submittal of vendor documents and to clearly distinguish the documents that are being submitted in each revision. The VPIS can undergo any number of revisions.
>
> Any deviations against PO and PO attachments shall be notified to CONTRACTOR for approval. A copy of the notification shall be marked to SUB-CONTRACTOR for information. However, VENDOR shall provide Technical explaination / justification for the same.

## SUB-CONTRACTOR'S Document Numbering Philosophy

> The SUB-CONTRACTOR's Number is made up of 4 alphanumeric fields, separated by dashes, as indicated here below:
>
> **[3863]{.underline}- [XX]{.underline}- [VD]{.underline}- [TT-UU-MMMM-NNNNNN-YYY]{.underline}**
>
> **Job EC Type N°**
>
> Job SUB-CONTRACTOR Job Number (4 digits), that is **3863**
>
> EC The EC field shall be equal to the one of the relevant MR
>
> Type always equal to VD
>
> N° identification number, composed as follows:
>
> TT : Vendor Document Typology Code (2 letters, as per [**Appendix 3**](#appendix---3-vendor-document-typology-and-codes)
>
> UU : Unit no.
>
> ABS Plant : **80**
>
> Rubber Plant : **85**
>
> Common Plant : **88**
>
> General (80/85/88) : **00**
>
> MMMM : The last 4 digits of the relevant MR from TCM document no.
>
> NNNNNN : Last 5 or 6 characters of equipment tag no. Identifying the item/material within the MR, for example the item code, or the position in the MR, or other.For MR relevant to bulk materials (piping, electrical, etc) this no shall be **000000.**
>
> Eg. 85-E-1701 **E1701**
>
> 85-PK-1170 **PK1170**
>
> Bulk Item **00000**
>
> YYY is a serial number (3 digits) (see Remarks)
>
> Remarks
>
> Serial number is made of 3 numeric characters without blank spaces or separators. Discipline Project Leaders shall define methodology consistent of each discipline and shall inform the VENDORS accordingly.
>
> ***[Example:]{.underline}***
>
> **3863-CE-VD-LG-85-0026-0E1701-001**
>
> Vendor General Arrangement of equipment 85-E-1701 which is in MR no. 3863-CE-MR-8500026 (CONTRACTOR MR J-85-ME-MRQ-0611-0001-0) from SUB-CONTRACTOR'S Static Equipment department.

## Documents / Drawings Revision Index

## Revision / Issue Number

> Each revision of Vendor documents shall be identified with a new revision index.
>
> Revision index shall be composed by 1 digits, and shall start from 0 (0, 1, 2, etc).
>
> Documents included in the Manufacturer's Data Book shall reflect the latest approved revision number without mark up and HOLDS.
>
> Revision Index to be updated with each submission.(see format)

## Indication of Revision

> Changes made to documents and drawing via revisions shall be clearly identified.
>
> Changes over drawings shall be "Clouded " with a revision triangle showing appropriate revision number(s) inside.
>
> Changes to documents shall be identified with: for text documents a vertical line on right side of the text modified; for datasheets, placing the appropriate revision number in the right / left hand revision column adjacent to the updated data.
>
> For the next document/drawing the highlighted revision, relevant the previous revision, shall be removed, the document/drawing revised and the highlighting for the current revision added.
>
> Where too many changes may impair the clarity/legibility, a note shall be provided on the document/drawing itself, stating "General Revision" and the reason of it. Such methodology is not acceptable for the documents already accepted or accepted with minor comments by CONTRACTOR.
>
> If document is re-submitted or revision of contents, the revision number must go up by one number.

## General Requirements for Document Preparation

## Language

> All VENDOR documents shall be provided in English language.

## Units of Measurements 

> All the Vendor's document must use the Imperial System units; International System unit can be used as secondary unit into brackets.

## File name of Electronic Documents

> This file must be named with the full document CONTRACTOR number and revision index, when applicable, as per the document numbering philosophy mentioned in section 4.3.1.
>
> *Example :*

**J-85-ME-DSH-0611-0001-001-0.pdf**

> All DOCUMENTS shall show the filename number, including revision code at the bottom of the front page close to Revision Table.

## Quality Requirements for Document Preparation

## Document Issue Purpose / Document Class

> All Vendor documents shall be submitted with the following issue purpose according to the stipulation of Requisition. The submission purpose shall be clearly indicated on the original paper of the documents and transmittal.
>
> IFA : Issued for Approval
>
> IFR : Issue For Review and comments
>
> IFI or Info : Issue for Information
>
> Final Issue : Document without Comments
>
> The VENDOR Document table included in the M.R. specifies the reason for transmission to CONTRACTOR / SUB-CONTRACTOR of the documents prepared by VENDOR. The codes shall be reported also on the VENDOR Document List as mentioned above.

## Coding of Approval Results

> Coding of approval will be as mentioned below:
>
> AP : Approved and released for manufacture, Vendor shall issue document as "FOR Final"
>
> CO : Not Approved. Corrected documents to be resubmitted before starting manufacture.
>
> Vendor shall revise Document and resubmit as "For Approval" or "For Review"
>
> RE : Rejected. Document shall be totally revised.
>
> NC : No Comment. Document was received for Information
>
> AC : Approved with Comments. Released for manufacture if change incorporated as
>
> indicated. Vendor shall revise Document and issue as "For Approval"

## Holds Management

> When details of a document/drawing have not been finalized, but the issue is required for other purposes, the area of the document/drawing not finalized shall be clearly identified as "HOLD".
>
> Details of each HOLD (such as owner, reason and date) shall be included in the General Notes section of the document/drawing under the heading of "HOLDS".

# VENDOR'S DOCUMENT TRANSMISSION FLOW

## General / Delivery Date

> All documents shall be delivered to the CONTRACTOR / SUB-CONTRACTOR by uploading the documents on FTP-Server.
>
> After a successful upload inside the FTP server, the VENDOR is required to send a Notification e-mail. The date of this e-mail shall be taken as reference for Document transmission.
>
> To fulfill the delivery schedule of the VENDOR's Documents agreed during the signature of the MRQ and reported in the SRQ, the transmission of the documents shall be considered effective when documents are received, as per the above indications.

## Electronic copies (FTP server)

> The electronic copies (pdf documents along with native files ) shall be uploaded into the FTP-Server by the VENDOR arranged for this Project by CONTRACTOR .
>
> It is mandatory that the VENDOR shall label the electronic files in accordance with the instructions reported inside this Specification (para. 4.3),
>
> The VENDOR shall upload the electronic copies along with the relevant transmittals.
>
> After a successful upload, the VENDOR shall mandatory notify the upload to the SUB-CONTRACTOR / CONTRACTOR document controller through an e-mail (notification e-mail) for his action.
>
> Uploads without the issue of a notification e-mail shall be considered as null.

## HEADING OF E-MAIL CORRESPONDENCE

> E-mail shall be deemed as formal correspondence. Vendor to include sequentially the following in their email correspondence :

-   Vendor Name

-   CONTRACTOR Purchase Order number or MR NO.

-   Transmittal no.

>
> All correspondence shall be sent in English language to person in charges in JSC & TCM
>
> Vendor shall immediately confirm verbal communications in writing to formalize matters.

## Review schedule 

> Document issued by VENDOR is notified to CONTRACTOR and SUB-CONTRACTOR as per section 5.4. CONTRACTOR shall provide comments if any, on the received vendor documents within 10 working days through a dedicated transmittal to SUB-CONTRACTOR.
>
> SUB-CONTRACTOR shall return documents sent as IFA / IFR , within 15 working days from the date of receiving soft copies, if not differently agreed in PO/MR.
>
> SUB-CONTRACTOR shall send consolidated comments to VENDOR ( This shall include the comments received from CONTRACTOR. )
>
> In case, the comments are not acceptable, VENDOR shall respond with the Technical explaination / justification for the disagreement, or request a meeting /Teleconference with SUB-CONTRACTOR / CONTRACTOR to solve the issue ASAP.

# HANDOVER OF FINAL DOCUMENTATION

> Final documentation is called as Manufacturer's data book (MDB) or Mechanical Catalogue shall be divided in three Parts for each equipment as separately:

1.  Part A - Engineering Dossier composed of :

-   All Fabrication drawings

-   Test Procedures

-   Welding Book

-   Fabrication Procedure

-   All relevant engineering documents specified in last column of Part II (Document and Drawing Supply) of this SRQ

2.  Part B - Manufacturer's Inspection data book or Inspection Dossier composed of :

-   All Test Reports

-   NDT Map

-   As-built drawings

-   All relevant inspection documents specified in last column of Part II (Document and Drawing Supply) of this SRQ\\

3.  Part C - Installation , Start-Up And Commissioning, Operation and Maintenance Manual

> VENDOR shall submit the index of contents of MDB for SUB-CONTRACTOR/CONTRACTOR approval within 4 weeks before the timing specified in the SRQ relevant to the issue of the final MDB.
>
> CONTRACTOR'S PO, MR number and the equipment number if applicable shall be shown on each document.
>
> Any section or sub-section not applicable to the equipment or item of material being supplied shall be marked "Not applicable" in the Index of Content. However, when a section or sub-section is completely not applicable, it shall be completely omitted. The DOCUMENTS present in each subsection shall be listed below the subsection title row.
>
> VENDOR shall then prepare one MASTER soft copy of MDB for SUB-CONTRACTOR/ CONTRACTOR review, before submitting the final required number of copies at the time specified in the SRQ.

# FORMAT FOR FINAL DOCUMENTATION 

## Hard Copies

> The drawings larger then A4 size shall be reduced (to A3 size preferably, if they remain readable, otherwise to A2) and/or folded to A4 size. All documents shall be then inserted into pre-punched plastic sleeves.
>
> All the VENDOR Documentation must be perfectly legible in all parts. Particular attention must be paid to certificates, reports and to any hand-written document.
>
> Binders shall be A4 size, 4-rings type, 70 mm (or 40mm) spine, PVC hard cover white colour, with transparent PVC jacket on cover and spine for cardboard label insert.
>
> Separator sheets will be white cardboard sheet, with right central label for indication of the section/subsection number.
>
> The front and spine of each binder (see Attachment-5 for front label and Attachment-6 for spine label) shall indicate the following as a minimum:

-   Project Name: ABS Rubber Project;

-   Client Reference: Jam Petrochemical Co.

-   Manufacturing Data Book (or Installation, Operating And Maintenance Manual or Equipment Certificate Dossier);

-   Discipline:

-   Equipment Tag No.;

-   Equipment Description;

-   Contractor's PO No.;

-   Material Requisition (MR) Number

-   Vendor Name;

-   Vendor Order No.;

-   Vendor Doc.No.;

-   CONTRACTOR Doc. No.

-   SUB-CONTRACTOR Doc. No.

-   Date of issue and Revision.

-   Volume Number (i.e. 1 of XX)

> Binder front and spine labels shall be printed on cardboard and inserted in the binder's front and spine transparent pocket.
>
> One hard copy of FINAL DOCUMENTATION shall be delivered jointly to shipped materials (even if the BUYER has not given final approval of MDB)

## Soft Copies / DATABASE

> All Soft Copies of the documents shall be identical to the relevant hard copies. All documentation shall be released in pdf file and in fully open and editable formats (Native Files) where applicable. The electronic files of Vendor catalogues and other not-modifiable documentation, such as test reports, certificates, shall be provided as pdf file, in case of catalogues, Standard Manuals and similar technical documentation, the pdf file shall be searchable to make easy the retrieval of the needed piece of information.
>
> Soft copies / Database of final documentation shall be provided as DVD.
>
> Soft copies of Part A / Part B / Part C shall be provided as DVD. One DVD may contain only one Part A or Part B or Part C. In case one Part A or Part B or Part C cannot be contained in one disk, each disk shall carry the indication "Disk n / N".
>
> Each DVD shall contain:

-   The general index of Part A / Part B / Part C with the links to the documents, sections must be provided. The Index of Content must be organized with the same document order requested for the Hard Copy.

-   All the required documentation (including the general index) in pdf format:

    -   pdf files for test reports or certificates shall be obtained by scanning; pdf files for all other DOCUMENTS (including catalogues, standard manuals and similar technical documentation) shall be obtained electronically and shall be searchable, to make easy the retrieval of the needed piece of information;

    -   The pdf files shall be merged to provide one pdf file corresponding to the contents of each volume (hard copy) or to more volumes, but without exceeding the size of 500 MB; the merged pdf file shall have hierarchically nested bookmarks to access the general index, the subsection covers and the single files;

    -   If some documents have a separate sub-index the same shall be created as bookmarks;

-   A separate directory named "Native Files" for the documents required also in open/editable formats, according the additional SRQ/MR requests, if any.

> Scanned files shall be generated with a minimum resolution of 200 dpi (dots per inch), or with a higher resolution when needed to ensure DOCUMENT perfect legibility. Black/white scan is acceptable for most applications, colour scan shall be utilized where needed for DOCUMENT comprehension.
>
> File names shall be according to 4.5.3.
>
> One soft copy of FINAL DOCUMENTATION shall be delivered jointly to shipped materials (even if the BUYER has not given final approval of MDB)
>
> DVD Label and DVD Box Label shall be respectively as per Attachment-7 and Attachment-8.
